title: Total tensor exactness and K-flatness for a flat-quotient short exact sequence
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and work with sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $0\to L^\bullet\xrightarrow{f}K^\bullet\xrightarrow{g}P^\bullet\to0$ be a sequence of integer-indexed cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] which is short exact in every degree, meaning $f^i$ is monic, $g^i$ is epic, and $\operatorname{im}(f^i)=\ker(g^i)$ for every $i\in\mathbf Z$. Suppose each $P^i$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For every cochain complex $A^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules, the induced sequence of direct-sum total tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]
$$0\to\operatorname{Tot}(L^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}A^\bullet)\xrightarrow{f\otimes1}\operatorname{Tot}(K^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}A^\bullet)\xrightarrow{g\otimes1}\operatorname{Tot}(P^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}A^\bullet)\to0$$
is short exact in every degree. If any two of $L^\bullet,K^\bullet,P^\bullet$ are K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], then the third is K-flat. No boundedness or degreewise splitting hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0G7B (lemma-K-flat-two-out-of-three-ses), statement and proof invoked in the K-flatness paragraph of Tag 0F1M

proof.text: Fix any complex $A^\bullet$. For each $p,q\in\mathbf Z$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-quotient-tensor-ses] to $0\to L^p\xrightarrow{f^p}K^p\xrightarrow{g^p}P^p\to0$ and $N=A^q$. The site is small, the rings are commutative, and the quotient $P^p$ is flat by hypothesis. Thus $0\to L^p\otimes A^q\to K^p\otimes A^q\to P^p\otimes A^q\to0$ is short exact as a sequence of sheaves, for every pair $(p,q)$. No flatness of $A^q$, $L^p$, or $K^p$ is required.

The same termwise conclusion holds with $A^q$ on the left. Indeed, for any module sheaf $M$, the sectionwise bilinear maps $m\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes m$ and $a\otimes m\mapsto m\otimes a$ give mutually inverse maps of presheaf tensor products, compatible with restrictions. Sheafifying gives $M\otimes A^q\cong A^q\otimes M$ by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. These maps commute with $f^p$ and $g^p$ on pure tensors, hence on the sheafified tensors. Transport the exact sequence of step 1 through these isomorphisms.

Fix $n\in\mathbf Z$ and let $I_n=\{(p,q)\in\mathbf Z^2:p+q=n\}$. By [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ is abelian, has small colimits, and filtered colimits are exact. A finite biproduct of short exact sequences is short exact: the kernel and cokernel universal properties are checked component by component in the finite biproduct. Apply this to each finite subset $J\subset I_n$ of the sequences in step 1. The finite subsets, ordered by inclusion, form a small filtered set (the empty subset is allowed and union gives an upper bound). Their colimit is the full coproduct: a compatible family of maps from finite subsums is exactly a family of maps from the individual summands. Exactness of filtered colimits therefore gives $0\to\bigoplus_{p+q=n}L^p\otimes A^q\to\bigoplus_{p+q=n}K^p\otimes A^q\to\bigoplus_{p+q=n}P^p\otimes A^q\to0$. The identical finite-subsum argument applied to step 2 gives the sequence with terms $\bigoplus_{q+p=n}A^q\otimes L^p$, and likewise for $K,P$. This uses sheaf coproducts, not sectionwise exactness or infinite products.

source.place: Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits), exact filtered colimits; finite-subsum expansion of the total-tensor assertion in sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0G7B

proof.text: By [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the first sequence in step 3 is exactly degree $n$ of the total tensor sequence in the statement. The maps commute with its differential: on the $(p,q)$ summand the differential is $d_M\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_A$ for $M=L,K,P$; the chain-map identities $f^{p+1}d_L^p=d_K^pf^p$ and $g^{p+1}d_K^p=d_P^pg^p$ give commutation with the first term, and tensor functoriality gives commutation with the second, with the same sign. Thus these are short exact sequences of complexes. In the left-tensor orientation the differential is $d_A\otimes1+(-1)^q1\otimes d_M$, and the same two identities show that $1\otimes f$ and $1\otimes g$ are chain maps. Step 3 proves exactness in every degree in that orientation too. Every differential has only two outgoing components per summand, so unboundedness causes no infinite-sum issue.

Now let $A^\bullet$ be acyclic and write $T_M=\operatorname{Tot}(A^\bullet\otimes M^\bullet)$ for $M=L,K,P$. By [def-pc-kflat-complex], K-flatness of any two of $L,K,P$ makes the corresponding two $T_M$ acyclic. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] to the left-tensor short exact sequence of step 4, in the abelian category $\Mod(\mathcal O)$. If $T_L,T_K$ are acyclic, exactness of $H^n(T_K)\to H^n(T_P)\to H^{n+1}(T_L)$ forces $H^n(T_P)=0$. If $T_K,T_P$ are acyclic, use $H^{n-1}(T_P)\to H^n(T_L)\to H^n(T_K)$; if $T_L,T_P$ are acyclic, use $H^n(T_L)\to H^n(T_K)\to H^n(T_P)$. In each case both neighboring objects vanish, so the middle object vanishes for every integer $n$. Thus the third $T_M$ is acyclic by [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules]. Since $A^\bullet$ was arbitrary acyclic, the definition [def-pc-kflat-complex] proves K-flatness of the third original complex. Together with step 4 this proves both assertions, with no boundedness or splitting assumption.

split_report.summary: Read Stacks 0G7B, 03EX, 03DB and 0117. Proved tensor exactness termwise, passed to total degrees using filtered finite subsums, checked both tensor orientations and chain-map signs, and proved all three K-flatness cases with the long exact cohomology sequence. Reused all supporting nodes; no new nodes and no statement changes.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the flat-quotient short-exact-sequence argument in the amplitude-to-model paragraph of lem-kun-0f1m (Stacks 0F1M via 0G7B). Current main-20261015 node has the same statement and no proof text; the stored source proof and current DAG parent identify this use.

The proof follows 0G7B. Step 1: termwise 03EX via lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-quotient-tensor-ses; its hypotheses (small site, commutative O, flat quotient P^p, arbitrary A^q) hold. Step 2: tensor swap for the left orientation that def-pc-kflat-complex needs. Step 3: the infinite total-degree coproduct is handled as a filtered colimit of finite biproducts, using the exact filtered colimits of lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian. Step 4: checked the chain-map signs in both orientations. Step 5: all three long-exact-sequence segments are correct, including the H^{n-1}(T_P)→H^n(T_L) shift. The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged from live, and live is still unsplit. There is no repair note, no new nodes, no cycle and no SGA citation. lem-kun-kflat-criteria(2) is two-out-of-three for triangles in K(Mod), not for a degreewise SES, so it is not a duplicate. The parent lem-kun-0f1m case (L,K K-flat ⇒ P) is covered. Accepted the declared tool_uses: generic 03EX and 03DB nodes that no node of the Künneth unit provides.
